notesStmt.note: Whitman created this manuscript in 1890, sometime between 27 June (the date of the verso letter) and November, when he submitted the poem for publication (see loc.00229).

This manuscript comprises trial lines for "Sail Out for Good, Eidólon Yacht!" which was published first in the March 1891 issue of Lippincott's Magazine, along with "Sounds of the Winter," "The Unexpress'd," and "After the Argument," under the general title "Old-Age Echoes." On the verso is a letter from Harry C. Kochersperger dated June 27, 1890.

lg.l: I will not call it my concluding voyayge
But entrance outset and true outset entrance of the whole them all.
Start out for good, and to return no more
